newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra stable.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra stable.

text.p: Indonesian coconut prices declined further on Friday amid poor market sentiment and thin buying interest, traders said.

"Buyers are not active and the poor market sentiment has forced coconut oil prices to continue falling. Based on my past experience, the market is always like this ahead of the elections," said one trader.

Traders said coconut oil was quoted at 1,750 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,790 rupiah/kg a week ago. Copra was stable at 800 rupiah/kg. Traders said players only bought what they needed immediately to avoid building up stocks.
The Indonesian general election campaign opens on Sunday and voting in the national and local elections is on May 29. The ruling Golkar party, in power for the last 30 years, is expected to win.
"The market is usually like this during the elections. It will become more and more quiet ahead of the polling day," said one trader.
Traders said many players were cautious over the possibility of social unrest during the campaign period. They believed that keeping their stocks as low as possible would limit risks.
"We expect demand from refineries to pick up again after the elections," said one trader.
"For the time being, copra producers continue doing their activities. They will later sell copra to refineries which need raw material for coconut oil," she said.
Manila traders said last Monday that growing coconut supply from both the Philippines and Indonesia should put a cap on the rise in coconut oil prices overseas.
Data released on Monday also showed coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam rose to 22,305 tonnes against 21,765 tonnes last week.
